2

Details

The X and Y lines both read the same pads; the resistive strips run along y, so landed charge spreads along y (the Y view’s slow RC component) but cannot spread across strips in x except over one strip’s own 550 µm width. Every study here uses the June 2026 bench (Ar/iso 95/5) except where SPS (det4, H4) is named.

3

Details

Q = √(q_x q_y)/path length, from the wft events (x_ok and y_ok, no spark) at the fitted (x_p0, y_p0), the median of ln Q in an anisotropic Gaussian kernel (2 mm across the X strips, 15 mm along them), relative to the chamber median. Cells with too few events are blank. The map is survivor-biased where nothing reconstructs (det4’s dead bands look less deep than they are); it is used to locate gradients, not as an efficiency map.

Median |Δ ln g| over 3 mm at a head-on event: det2 0.06, det3 0.05, det4 0.30, det6 0.06, det7 0.09. det4 is the chamber with 2–38 mm dead stripes along X (det4_sps_assessment); its gain changes by ~35 % within a width-stack window at a typical event.

Built by gainmap_export.py → results/gain_maps.json, from strip_gain_audit.gain_map.

4

Details

Head-on test (this morning): the median ratio of a channel’s peak to the cluster maximum when it sits at ±1 (unsaturated events, peak 200–3500 ADC), plus the rate of clearing 5σ next to a cluster (also on saturated events). It judges only the channels the head-on sample passes over: 31–85 of 512 on det2, det6 and det7, where most head-on events saturate.

Inclined test (added this afternoon, strip_gain_audit.holes): in the inclined-track caches every strip whose two spatial neighbours both fire (unsaturated) should read about as much as their mean; the median of peak / neighbours’ mean per channel, dead below 0.25 × the chamber median. It is blind to noise (a noisy channel’s higher 5σ threshold made a first firing-rate version flag ~50 live det7 channels) and judges 190–500 channels.

Where both judge they agree (det3 307; det6’s alternating 36–62 / 208 / 224 / 388–392). New from the inclined test: det7 ~20 dead X channels in 67–250, det2 69 and 269, det3 39, det4 eight more. det6’s connector pattern (even channels, pairs) and Y channels 7 and 9 dead on both det6 and det7 point to the readout cabling rather than the boards. Every flagged channel (strip_gain_audit.bad_set) is now masked by the gap profile and by the stacks (rc_diffusion.annotate_bad).

5

Details

det4 head-on events with window maximum below 1000 ADC sit at local gain e^−0.66 and 71 % of them have a dead or weak strip within ±4; above 3500 they sit at e^+1.1 (48 %). Tightening the saturation cut keeps the faint ones, which are the ones next to dead strips, so the cut walked the sample onto the bad strips.

The model-free ratio r is 0.43–0.48 at every amplitude on clean windows (the uniform-gain toy gives 0.44–0.47), and 0.27–0.37 when a dead/weak strip sits in ±2. With σ0 fixed at 0.35 mm the clean-window D_T is flat in the cut (413 / 409 / 396 / 420 at 3500 / 2500 / 2000 / 1500 ADC, GAP-30 frame; reproduced and stored this afternoon as g_det4@g99@s00.35, XW_MIN_EV=60), and so is the D_T of the windows with a bad strip, ~130 lower (282 / 277 / 266 / 278). The all-event cut dependence is the mix of the two changing with the cut. With σ0 free, σ0 rises 0.43 → 0.51 as D_T falls 354 → 280 (clean): the two trade within errors.

Masking only the flagged strips (NaN in the stack) is not enough: det4 widens to 378 ± 23 but stays cut-dependent, because its gain falls over the band edges around the dead strips. det4 widths need the clean-window selection.

What had to be done with the dead strips: (1) flag them per chamber from the data themselves (strip_gain_audit.py, per-event flags in gainflags_<key>.pkl); (2) mask them in every stack (rc_diffusion.annotate_bad, unsat_width.py --mask) and out of the gap profile’s charge and exposure; (3) for det4, keep only windows with no flagged strip in ±4 and a small gain gradient. Still to do: the closure toy with the same masks, and the SPS run_71 det4 stacks (beam channel numbering).

gap_extent.py → results/gap_extent.json; closure toy gap_extent_toy.py

6

Details

Every earlier gap was a drift time times a velocity (T_end × v), carrying a ±1 mm kernel systematic and a strong amplitude dependence (det4 +9 mm). Here no time enters: the X strip at x collects the ionisation from depth z = (x − x_mesh)/tan_ref over a slice pitch/|tan| thick. The half-height points of a smeared step stay where the step is for any symmetric blur (footprint, diffusion, reference error, the strip’s own z interval, and a mixture of them over the tan range). An x_mesh error moves both edges together and leaves the gap.

Closure (toy with Fischle clusters, Polya gain, Magboltz-size diffusion, the bundle template at the data’s peak sample, 60 ns sampling, noise, reference smear): G = 30 returns 30.0–30.1 at v = 26–38 µm/ns; G = 27.9 returns 27.75. The peak-sample variant reads +0.6 to +2.3 mm high (blur-dependent) and is not used. Normalising each event to its own plateau instead of its total let a few mis-referenced events dominate (an early det3 pass read 30.2; superseded).

The M3 slope scale is not included: the gap scales as 1/scale.

7

Details

Two selections (afternoon, §39): the morning’s numbers dropped every event with a saturated sample, which left det2 148 and det7 139 tracks. gap_extent.py --satmask keeps those events and masks only their clipped strips (out of charge and exposure, normalisation scaled by the good fraction of the column). det3 reads the same (28.10 → 28.06); det2 and det4 read 0.6 and 0.4 mm shorter, det7 1.2 mm longer. The adopted value is the mean, with half the difference added to the error. The morning’s det7 30.1 also lost 20 newly flagged dead strips (28.2 on its long run with them masked).

det3’s short gap agrees with its timing value (28.1 ± 0.2 against 27.9) now that one of the two does not depend on any kernel. det2 − det3 = +3.4 mm, as the timing contrast said (+2.8 to +3.4). det4’s timing value (25.6) was the amplitude/dead-strip problem of §35.

det2’s +tan and −tan halves differ by 2.4 mm, which a drift-field or reference tilt of tan ≈ 0.012 does; the mean is first-order free of it. det3’s halves differ by 0.9 mm (δ ≈ 0.005).

det6 cannot be measured this way: its deep charge runs past the 32-sample window (the deep strips’ last sample is at 40–86 % of their peak), so its value is a lower limit and gaps.py keeps 30 ± 2. det3 on 6-22 (8.9 µm/ns that night) is excluded for the same reason, and so is det3 at 700 V drift.

Effect on the width comparison (no refit): det3 unchanged (+230 µm/√cm at 347 V/cm, 7.8 sd); det7 now sits on Magboltz (+88, 0.3 sd); det2 is two-valued (0.09 % water −228 or 0.65 % +188, ~1 sd each); det4 +62 (0.3 sd).

Saturated pulses: the censored fit is as good as on bright unclipped ones

det3 X residuals of the rcms25 forward model, at the clipped strip (left) and its ±1 neighbours (right)

saturated

bright, unsaturated

sat_residual.py → results/sat_residual_det3.json; production censors samples ≥ 3550 ADC with a one-sided penalty

8

Details

On det3 saturated events carry 4–6× the χ²/dof of unsaturated ones in every kernel (X production 186 vs 32). That is brightness, not clipping: the residual just before and after the clipped run (+0.073, +0.059 at k = +1, +0.019 at +2, −0.014 at +5) is the same as around the peak of bright unsaturated strips (+0.061 / +0.055 / +0.022 / −0.029): a template mismatch that grows with amplitude (MODEL_FRAC is the existing handle). No recovery tail, baseline shift or neighbour pick-up shows after the clip.

So per event the forward model uses saturated pulses as well as the data allow. The stack studies are what cannot: a stack has no per-sample censoring, so they drop saturated events — 70–85 % of det2/det6/det7 — and on a chamber with gain structure that selects low-gain regions (§35). The answer is a per-event censored width fit, below.

9

Details

The RC kernel’s X χ²/dof is worse than production’s on every chamber (det3 58 → 79). The deficit is uniform (×1.2–1.4) on unsaturated, saturated, head-on, inclined and faint events, so it is not saturation. By strip offset the RC model under-predicts the centre and over-predicts ±1: its footprint is too wide. Lorentzian tails make it worse.

Resolution (scale-corrected s68 against production, blind start): narrowing σ0_x never costs overall X resolution (det3 +0.005 → +0.013 ± 0.019°), moves every angle slope toward 1 by 0.007–0.030, and removes most of det4’s X deficit (+0.164 → +0.061 ± 0.044°). Head-on, the wide footprint is still worth something on det7 (−0.16 vs −0.06) and det3 (+0.01 vs +0.04).

The per-event fit wants σ0_x ≈ 0.20–0.25 mm where the head-on stacks measure 0.35–0.43. The next slides take up whether that makes physical sense, and the left-over asymmetry.

The det3 drift scan meshes: one water fits every field, at the gap the charge extent gives

det3 6-27, v = gap / T of the unsaturated head-on stacks against Magboltz; right: the gap the scan alone prefers

vdrift_consistency.py → results/vdrift_consistency.json; Magboltz air_hs grid (Ar/iso 95/5 + water); E = V / gap (was V / 2.88 cm for every chamber)

10

Details

T is the charge column’s arrival length from the stack fit (x_width.fit_x, T free), with its bootstrap error and a 1.5 % systematic per stack. The six points are the 700 / 900 / 1100 V scan sub-runs, the 1000 V long run and the two 1000 V amplification-scan points (mesh 445 / 465 V), which must and do agree with each other. The 500 V and lower sub-runs are window-limited (no drift end inside 1.9 µs) and carry no v.

Water and gap are not degenerate here because v(E) in Ar/iso changes shape with water: at ~1 % it still rises steeply at 250 V/cm and flattens by 390. Profiling the gap (water refitted at each) gives the minimum at 28.25 mm, against the timing-free 28.08 ± 0.19: two estimates with nothing in common but the data.

The beam cannot do the same for det4. The run_63 ladder v (7.77 / 5.83 / 4.04 µm/ns) is a ratio of loss rates per ns and per mm on strip peak times; the peak-time ladder itself reads 10.0 µm/ns at the same field (angled_kernel), the 20–30 % compression of RECONSTRUCTION_BASIS. With either, ladder + Magboltz + the run_71 drift end returns a gap independent of the one assumed (28.6 mm with 7.77), so the beam carries no gap information at the 1 mm level. It also means the beam composition fit’s low-field v constraint is weaker than its quoted 3 %.

vdrift_consistency.py; D_T from unsat_width.py (unsaturated head-on stacks), rescaled × √(30/gap)

11

Details

A chamber with one field has one free gas parameter (water) per run, so v alone cannot test the gap. Diffusion can: the measured D_T falls as √(30/gap) with the assumed gap, while the Magboltz D_T at the water that v implies rises (a longer gap means a faster v, so a drier gas, so more diffusion). Where they cross is a gap from timing and diffusion together. det2 crosses at 31.3 mm (timing-free 31.1), det4 at 30.5 (30.5), det7’s long run at 30.0 (29.4; its longer run 32.3 and HV pool 27.2 scatter by ±2.5). The crossing is shallow, ±1–2 mm per chamber.

det3 is the exception: its D_T would need a 31 mm gap, where the scan and the charge extent both say 28.1. Its excess is +160 to +260 µm/√cm in quadrature at every field of the scan (249–392 V/cm) at the scan’s own water: a constant extra transverse spread per unit drift length on that chamber, not a gap or a field effect.

det6 and det7 ran side by side (6-26, same run, same field) and their v implies 0.8–0.9 % and 0.4–0.6 % water. The gas was not the same in the two chambers, or det6’s stack T is biased by its window-limited deep charge. Per-chamber water is consistent with the 10-08 synthesis (water ingress local to each chamber, x·Q ≈ const). det7’s long and longer runs differ by 4σ in v (water drifting over the night).

Clipping unsaturated pulses on purpose: censoring keeps the angle, loses some charge

det3 and det2, 540–740 bright unclipped events clipped at 0.4 / 0.6 × their maximum (4–6-sample runs, like real ones)

sat_closure.py → results/sat_closure_.json; bars: det3 then det2, darker = clip at 0.6; production bundle, reference start

12

Details

The question: should saturated pulses be reconstructed from the slopes on either side, with a larger uncertainty on the interpolated samples? What production does is the limit of that idea: the clipped samples are left out of the charge solve, so the pulse template fitted to the unclipped rising and falling edges fills the peak, and a one-sided penalty is added wherever the model falls below the clip. Nothing is interpolated by hand, and no error has to be invented for interpolated samples.

The test takes events with no saturation (window max 1500–3400 ADC) and clips them at a fraction of their own maximum, so the truth is the same event unclipped. Four treatments: production censoring; the bound model ≥ clip enforced inside the solve (new, wft.model.SAT_SOLVE, opt-in; an active set as in a Tobit fit); clipped samples taken at face value; strips with a clipped sample dropped.

Result: censoring moves the angle by s68 0.003–0.005 in tan against a 0.018–0.021 resolution, and the resolution against M3 is unchanged. Taking clipped samples at face value doubles the position scatter and loses 10–27 % of the charge; dropping the strips is far worse. The charge of censored fits reads 6–12 % low, and the in-solve bound only recovers 1–3 points of that: the deficit is the template under-filling bright pulses (the same +6–7 % peak residual seen on bright unclipped strips, §37), not the censoring.

Next for saturation: an amplitude-dependent pulse template, measured from bright unclipped pulses; then the charge (dE/dx, gain maps) of saturated events is usable. Angles and positions already are.

Layer numbers from docs/detector_spec (several from memory, flagged open there); D_rc per chamber from the RC arms (2.8–7.9e-4 mm²/ns)

13

Details

Does narrowing σ0_x make physical sense? Yes. The model already integrates each landing over the 0.78 mm pitch (that alone is σ = 0.225 mm), so σ0 is only what the charge adds beyond it. The avalanche is tiny (≈ 25 µm over the 150 µm gap, Magboltz). Induction through the ≈ 70 µm kapton + glue onto 0.68 mm pads adds of order the insulator thickness. The one large term is the resistive strip itself: charge landed on a 550 µm strip spreads across its width until it fills it, a box of σ = 0.55/√12 = 0.16 mm. In quadrature, ≈ 0.18–0.2 mm.

Is it different from Y? It should be. Along y the landed charge keeps spreading along the strip (RC diffusion, width² += 2 D_rc t, the slow component the RC kernel models); across it, in x, the spread stops at the strip edges. So Y’s effective width is dominated by RC from the first tens of ns, X’s by one bounded box.

How fast is the spread across the strip? The same RC constant governs it: τ ≈ (w/2)² / D_rc = 0.0756 mm² / (2.8–7.9e-4 mm²/ns) ≈ 95–270 ns per chamber. That is inside the shaping time, which is why X has a small slow part too, and it is the time scale of the one-sided copy on the next slide (measured 105–120 ns).

Why the stacks read wider: a head-on stack’s ±1 charge includes that one-sided delayed copy and, for |tan| < 0.03, ~0.1 mm of track walk (§30); a symmetric Gaussian fitted to it widens to cover both.

xasym_tests.py, xasym_samechannel.py, xasym_boundary.py → results/xasym_*.json; raw windows, no template or kernel

14

Details

Model-free throughout: raw waveform windows (rows in position order), unsaturated, no flagged strip within ±2.

Not a walk. A drift walk (a tilt between the field, the chamber and the reference) makes the two neighbours differ in timing. The ±1 mean-time difference crosses zero at tan_ref ≈ −0.005 on det3, the same 0.005 offset its ±tan gap halves gave. At that angle the timing is symmetric, yet Q₋₁ exceeds Q₊₁ by +0.165 ± 0.019 (head-on, aQ = (Q₋₁ − Q₊₁)/(Q₋₁ + Q₊₁)). The −1 minus +1 difference is 0.13 × the centre pulse delayed by ≈ 114 ns (89 % of it explained); det4 bench 105 ns, det7 120 ns (n 20). H4 had “−1 delayed 112 ns, +1 prompt”.

Not the strip gains. On the beam, aQ follows position (−0.27 at x ≈ 105, 0.00 at 155, +0.31…+0.39 at 185–215 mm): det4’s strip-scale gain swings dominate a cluster-level ratio there. The gain-free test compares each channel with itself: its share of the cluster when it is the −1 neighbour against when it is the +1 neighbour. Median over 56 channels +0.43 ± 0.08; a toy with symmetric sharing and a ×3 random (uncorrelated) gain spread analysed the same way gives −0.05…0.00. But A is not one number: it is ≈ 0 over the whole 149–161 mm band (chip 1, local 48–63) and +0.4…+0.75 over 182–214 mm (chip 1 local 6–22 and chip 2). Same chip, different band, different answer, so it is not a chip property; but det4’s gain changes ×20 across its 12 mm live bands, and a gradient that size enters the cluster normalisation, so the beam test is not clean. It is inconclusive, not evidence either way. On the bench, with uniform illumination, the cluster-level aQ is already gain-averaged: det3 +0.17 ± 0.02, det2 +0.07 ± 0.04, det4 +0.07 ± 0.03, det7 +0.19 ± 0.07, det6 -0.02 ± 0.07. Same sign on four of five; size per chamber.

Independent check: the raw-ADC study published the same day (notes/det3-x-asymmetry, NB_ASYM.md; no strip map, no common mode, its own extractor) finds the same copy into the lower-position neighbour, on det3’s June-15 build X view only (84 % of events against 50 % on every other board and view), strongest mid-board, changing with drift field; it rules out the code and the FEU slot, and finds the one known board asymmetry (one-sided bus traces under the checkerboard pads) ten times too weak. My bench det2/det4/det7 numbers above are 2–2.7σ and do not contradict its 50 %.

Not a pitch beat. An 800 µm resistive pitch over 780 µm pads would modulate the asymmetry with a 31.2 mm period; the periodogram has no peak there (power 0.4–7 against a null mean of 2) or anywhere else significant.

Electronics crosstalk: not settled by these data. Channel numbers fall with +x in every 64-channel block on all chambers, so position and channel order never separate except at chip edges, where spatial neighbours sit on different chips. On the beam, clusters centred on the four edge strips give aQ −0.31, +0.39, +0.27, −0.02: dominated by those strips’ gains, so not decisive. A separate study of quiet events in raw data (nb_asym_raw, 19 Oct) is looking at channel-to-channel pick-up directly.

A candidate explanation for the X asymmetry, offered to the simulation side

A hypothesis with tests, not a result

Established. det3 (June-15 build): a one-sided X neighbour copy, delayed ~110 ns, in raw waveforms, 8σ, confirmed by the independent raw-ADC note (det3-x-asymmetry); other boards at most 2–3σ; Y symmetric.

Candidate mechanism. the resistive strips offset from the pad columns (slide 13, ③): Y’s RC spread, seen in X where a strip overlaps one neighbouring pad.

Tests that need no new data. a stack-up simulation with a plausible δ (the bus traces alone are ×10 too weak); the copy’s delay against det3’s own D_rc at each drift field; why only one board (its print registration).

Not claimed. as a model term. Production’s c1_asym stays an effective parameter until those agree.

15

Details

Delays measured (det3 114, det4 105, det7 120 ns) against τ = (0.275 mm)² / D_rc from each chamber’s RC arm (det3 272, det4 270, det7 132, det2 180, det6 95 ns): the same order, shorter by up to ×2.5 on det3/det4, as expected if the overlap begins inside the strip half-width. Not a fit; D_rc is itself a bench-fitted effective constant.

Predictions: a fixed sign per board; size set by the screen-print registration δ (tens of µm), so chamber-dependent and possibly varying across a board (det3’s aQ ranges 0.05–0.34 along x); no effect in Y (its strips run along the resistive strips); a 31.2 mm beat if the resistive pitch were 800 µm against the 780 µm pads. No beat is seen, which is weak evidence that the pitches match (docs/detector_spec q_esl_geom: 800 µm was from memory).

Electronics crosstalk is not excluded: channel order follows position everywhere except chip edges, and the chip-edge test on det4 is dominated by the gain structure.

What this does not rule out

Open after 19 Oct

det3’s D_T excess. +160 to +260 µm/√cm at every field, at the gap both timing and charge extent agree on. Not the gap, not the field, not saturation. Unexplained.

det6. its gap is not measurable (window), and its v implies a different water from det7’s in the same run.

The beam gap of det4. not testable: the ladder v is estimator-dependent by 25 %, and the beam water’s low-field constraint inherits it.

The X asymmetry. real in the data; the mechanism is a hypothesis. Electronics crosstalk is not excluded by these tests.

Charge of saturated events. 6–12 % low until the pulse template depends on amplitude.

The M3 slope scale. every timing-free gap scales as 1/scale; not in the errors.
